newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kloeckner broke even in first four months.
newsitem.headline: Kloeckner broke even in first four months.

text.p: German engineering group Kloeckner Werke AG said on Monday it broke even in the first four months of the business year 1996/97, compared to a loss of 16 million marks ($9.5 million) in the same period a year ago.
Sales in the period rose slightly to 1.3 billion marks. New orders for the first four months also increased slightly to 1.4 billion marks.
Kloeckner also said it expected operating profit for the full year to at least remain unchanged from the 49.3 million marks it earned last year.
"This year should be a year of stabilisation," chief executive Heinz-Ludwig Schmitz said at a news conference. "The results of ordinary activities should reach at least the same level as last year."

The sale of Kloeckner's Kautex-Gruppe, a maker of plastic fuel tanks, and the consolidation of its Kalle plastic films business into a joint venuture had changed the structure of group revenue, Schmitz said.

Its automobile supply unit now generated 40 percent of sales, down from 55 percent, while its plastics unit provided 20 percent of revenue, up from 13 percent. Bottling and packaging technology continued to supply 30 percent, he said.
In the first four months of 1996/97, automotive sales were rising and plastics business was "encouraging," Schmitz said. Bottling and packaging was about level with the first four months of 1995/96
Kloeckner expected 1996/97 sales of about four billion marks compared to 4.5 billion marks the previous year, Schmitz said. It has about 16,000 employees, down from 18,298.
Kloeckner last year sold Kautex to Textron Inc. Kalle Hartfolien GmbH jointed with a Hoeschst AG unit, Pentaplast GmbH, to form Kalle Pentaplast GmbH.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.692 German Marks)
